document.title: Usama bin Ladin: Pressing High-Level Taliban Official Jalaluddin Haqqani on Bin Ladin (State 095538)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Secret, NODIS] U.S. officials meet directly with Jalaluddin Haqqani, Acting Minister of Borders, to discuss bin Ladin. Haqqani is described as a key official with links to Arab militants. He is appreciative of U.S. aid during the anti-Soviet jihad but resentful of the August 1998 missile strike on a Haqqani-linked camp in Khost. U.S. officials warn the U.S. will keep making things difficult for the Taliban unless bin Ladin is expelled. Haqqani agrees bin Ladin is 'a problem' but suggests the best solution is for him to remain in the country.

events.description: US Embassy political officer met Jalaluddin Haqqani and urged expulsion of Bin Ladin; Haqqani said the Taliban hold him under control and urged talks.
US cruise missile strike on Bin Ladin-linked facilities in Khost, destroying Haqqani's base and madrasa and killing 25 mujahideen per Haqqani.
Cable Islamabad 4099 reporting the meeting, relayed by State as 095538.
US cruise missile strike on Bin Ladin-linked facilities in Khost Province, destroying Haqqani-linked base and madrassah; Haqqani claimed 25 mujahideen killed.
US Embassy political officer met Jalaluddin Haqqani, urging Taliban to expel Bin Ladin; Haqqani urged continued talks and asked US to stop pressuring Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
Islamabad cable 4099 reporting the Haqqani meeting sent to State and repeated to Abu Dhabi, Lahore, Peshawar, Riyadh.
East Africa embassy bombings attributed to Bin Ladin, leaving well over 200 dead, cited by US as reason for demanding expulsion.

key_claims: Haqqani was a Taliban Acting Minister of Borders and Kabul-sector commander in May 1999.
The US assessed Haqqani as having close ties to Arab and Kashmiri militants whose Khost facilities were hit in August 1998.
Haqqani said his base, madrasa and 25 mujahideen were lost in the US strike.
Haqqani echoed the Taliban line that Bin Ladin was under control and the US had offered no proof of guilt.
Haqqani asked the US to stop pressuring Saudi Arabia and the UAE, suggesting Taliban isolation was biting.
Haqqani met US officials quietly because the Taliban did not want him meeting foreigners.
